segments.strap: HEARTBEAT NEWS
segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: Nvidia's boss is back, tankers burn near Hormuz, and a nuclear satellite warning rattles NATO
bullets: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang; stocks surge, and the U.S. blacklists Megaspeed
Iran claims three tankers hit mines; Washington widens sanctions
NATO warns on a reported Russian nuclear satellite
Army to detonate toxic lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Tuesday, November twenty-fourth. Nvidia's board has taken its chief executive back, a week after he left. Stock markets from Taipei to New York jumped.

In the Gulf, Iran says three tankers hit mines. The United States answered with more sanctions. And NATO's chief says the alliance will defend against threats in space, after reports that Russia may be preparing a nuclear-armed satellite.
At home, a congressman resigns, the Army plans a big controlled blast in Iowa, and the House Democrats pile up their biggest majority since nineteen ninety-two. Plenty more. Let's go.

segments.strap: NVIDIA TAKES JENSEN HUANG BACK AS CEO
segments.headline: A week after he resigned, Huang is reinstated

stats.label: Board action
stats.value: Unanimous reinstatement as president, CEO, director (8-K)

lines.text: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and director. That is from the company's own filing. He resigned on November twelfth. Reports last week said the chair did not intend to bring him back.

So the plan was no plan, and then the plan was yes. Nvidia says it consulted senior U.S. government officials and concluded his return posed no national-security risk. The White House says President Trump was, quote, totally involved.

Markets loved it. A.P. reports Monday closes of S&P five hundred up four point seven percent, Nasdaq up six point five, Dow up three. France twenty-four puts Nvidia's own gain at thirty-one point five percent. In Asia, A.P. had Taiwan's index up more than nine percent, Korea's Kospi up six point five, and Japan's Nikkei up three point nine, at reported times, not certified closes.
Experts on the B.B.C. called it the biggest U-turn in economic history. That is their phrase, and it is a lot of history.

Not everything is solved. Analysts say the rally is relief about continuity for the A.I. buildout. The board investigation, the company's financing commitments to customers and suppliers, and possible congressional inquiries remain open. Separately, the U.S. added Megaspeed, the A.I. firm at the center of the Nvidia scandal, to its trade blacklist on Monday.
So: the boss is back, and the blacklist is bigger. Both are true on the same day.

segments.strap: IRAN CLAIMS THREE TANKERS HIT MINES
segments.headline: Hormuz: Iran's claims, Washington's sanctions

stats.label: Iran's claim
stats.value: Three tankers hit mines despite U.S. escort (IRGC)

sources.name: Al Jazeera (Iran vows to counter blockade)
State Department (Rubio and Qatar's prime minister)

lines.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy says three oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, despite a U.S. escort. One near the southern coast, two in the eastern strait. No ship names, and no independent confirmation in the reports we reviewed. That is Iran's claim.

Iran also says it shot down a U.S. drone near the strait, and vows to end the American naval blockade by, quote, all available means. Those are Iranian statements. Washington has not been quoted on the drone.

The U.S. side. Treasury sanctioned twenty-two entities and eight people linked to Iran, plus dozens tied to shadow banking networks. Vice President Vance and Secretary of State Rubio met Qatar's prime minister. A.P. says no new policy direction was announced.
There is also a claim that President Trump postponed possible Iran strikes until January first, and that they could resume if talks fail. That comes from a market report, not the White House.
Oil did not panic. Brent is near eighty-eight dollars and seventy cents, close to a three-month low. Reuters says rising supply is outweighing the Hormuz risk.
Two sides, one strait, and a lot of unconfirmed fire. We will keep both accounts.

segments.strap: REPORTS: IRAN EXPANDING CHEMICAL, BIO PROGRAMS
segments.headline: U.S. intelligence claims, and Iran's denial

stats.label: The claim
stats.value: U.S. intelligence believes Iran is expanding chemical and biological weapons (reports)

stats.label: Also reported
stats.value: Iran may be considering a radiological 'dirty bomb' attack on U.S. officials

stats.label: Shipping cyberattacks
stats.value: U.S. eyes Iran as possible culprit (WSJ)

lines.text: Reports say U.S. intelligence believes Iran is expanding its chemical and biological weapons capabilities, and may be considering a radiological dirty bomb attack against U.S. officials. This is reported intelligence, from two outlets, not a government announcement.
Iran rejects the allegations that it is developing biological or chemical weapons. Nothing in what we read shows a specific plot or a date.

Also, the Wall Street Journal reports that U.S. authorities are looking at Iran, or possibly Russia, as the source of dozens of cyberattacks and threats aimed at as many as fifty tankers. Neither attribution is confirmed.

segments.strap: NATO WARNS ON RUSSIAN NUCLEAR SATELLITE
segments.headline: Alliance vows to defend space as reports warn of a launch

stats.label: NATO's Rutte
stats.value: Alliance will defend against threats in space

stats.label: Status
stats.value: Reports, not an official Russian action

stats.label: Poland
stats.value: NATO to supply an early-warning aircraft

lines.text: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte says the alliance will defend against threats in space. That follows reports that Russia may be preparing to launch a satellite carrying a nuclear weapon. Germany is quoted as warning it could happen within sixty days.
To be clear, these are reports and warnings from allies. We found no Russian announcement. Ars Technica says it could come sooner than first thought.
Related, and also on the wire: a Fox News report quotes Russia's Dmitry Medvedev warning of a, quote, preventive nuclear attack, claiming Ukraine and NATO crossed a line. One outlet. A claim.

On the ground, NATO will provide an early-warning aircraft to Poland after Russian missiles reportedly landed there. Poland also says a Russian drone briefly entered its airspace overnight. And Moscow accuses Estonia of hostile actions on the, quote, verge of triggering open war. Russia's words.
President Trump meets Rutte on Wednesday, the White House says.

segments.strap: UKRAINE: LIBYA SHIP CLAIMS, NEW STRIKES
segments.headline: Russia launches 134 drones; Tripoli wants answers from Kyiv

stats.label: Merkury
stats.value: Zelensky: sunk. Libyan officials: severely damaged

lines.text: An update on the Libya strike. President Zelensky says seven Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi, and also hit the cargo ship Angara and destroyed a helicopter. Libyan officials say the Merkury was severely damaged, not sunk, with at least ten wounded.

Now Libya's Tripoli government wants an explanation from Kyiv for striking Russian ships in Libyan waters. A think tank analyst says it is hard to imagine Tripoli approving it. Russia has not been quoted confirming the loss.

Overnight, Russia launched one hundred thirty-four drones at Ukraine, according to a report citing officials. Ukrainian officials say a Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia killed at least two and hurt thirty-three. Ukraine keeps hitting Russian oil sites. Russian officials say a Rostov refinery halted after a long attack.

On diplomacy, Zelensky said Kyiv is ready to talk with Europe, the United States and Russia as early as tomorrow. No date. No agenda. And the Financial Times says the Pentagon has delayed Patriot missile shipments already allocated to Ukraine. Zelensky has asked again for those decisions.

segments.strap: KOREA ALERT, HASINA'S RETURN, AND MORE FROM ASIA
segments.headline: Ulleung shelter warning; a death sentence in China

stats.label: Ulleung Island
stats.value: Brief shelter warning; aircraft identity disputed

stats.label: China
stats.value: Official 'Ma' sentenced to death for spying

sources.name: Japan Times (Russian aircraft in air defense zone)

lines.text: South Korea briefly told residents of Ulleung Island to take shelter after aircraft approached. Outlets disagree on what the aircraft was. One says a suspected North Korean aircraft breached the island's airspace. The Guardian and others say Russian military aircraft. Seoul also says several Russian aircraft flew into its air defense zone.
So: a shelter warning, two possible culprits, and no one hurt in what we read. We will update when Seoul is specific.

In Bangladesh, a spokesperson says ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return from exile in India on December sixteenth. A Bangladeshi minister said she would return, quote, in handcuffs. No return has happened.

China says an official named Ma was sentenced to death for sending state secrets to a foreign handler. The account comes from a state-affiliated source. India pledged one point six billion dollars to Nepal after its floods. And North Korea says it is considering shutting down a Swiss diplomatic office in Pyongyang.

Also, Taiwan holds local elections soon, and Beijing is already attacking the ruling party's candidate. Unnamed sources told the Sydney Morning Herald that the Solomon Islands will not renew its China security pact. Neither Canberra nor Beijing has confirmed that.

segments.strap: GAZA STRIKES KILL AT LEAST THREE, INCLUDING UN WORKER
segments.headline: Israeli strikes, a Yemen toll, and a West Bank report

graphic.title: Gaza, Yemen and the West Bank

stats.label: Gaza
stats.value: At least 3 killed incl. an UNRWA worker (reports)

stats.label: Israel politics
stats.value: Netanyahu and Eisenkot spar over Iran threat

lines.text: Israeli drone strikes in Gaza killed at least three people, including a worker for the U.N. agency UNRWA, according to Al Jazeera and Reuters. Anadolu says one strike hit a police post in the south and wounded five more.
In Yemen, Houthi authorities say coalition strikes killed eleven people and wounded nineteen in the west of the country. That is the Houthi account.

Al Jazeera reports that so-called military zones in the occupied West Bank are becoming de facto Israeli settler land. In Israel, opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot and Prime Minister Netanyahu are arguing over whether Iran is an, quote, immediate threat.

One small sign of normal: flydubai has been approved to resume flights to Tel Aviv, two months after a thwarted attack. And in Iran, a singer and four others reportedly received lashes after a concert without a hijab. The Guardian and Times of Israel both report it.

segments.strap: GOMEZ RESIGNS; DEMOCRATS HIT 258 HOUSE SEATS
segments.headline: Congress, courts and a feud with Newsom

stats.label: Rep. Jimmy Gomez
stats.value: Resigning after Ethics finding of sexual misconduct

stats.label: California ballots
stats.value: Appeals court OKs DOJ dropping its suit

stats.label: Trump hush-money case
stats.value: Appeals court allows another federal-court bid

sources.name: NBC News live blog (House seats, Alaska)

lines.text: California Democrat Jimmy Gomez says he will resign after a House Ethics Committee found evidence of sexual misconduct. NBC and the Guardian both report it. Perplexity adds that the committee reported misconduct by three outgoing lawmakers, including campaign-finance violations and misuse of taxpayer funds.

On the numbers, NBC reports Democrats have secured at least two hundred fifty-eight House seats, their largest majority since nineteen ninety-two, after Chuck Hubbard beat Virginia Foxx in North Carolina. Alaska certified Democrat Mary Peltola's Senate win.

In court, a federal appeals court approved the Justice Department's dismissal of its lawsuit over about twenty thousand California ballots. A different appeals court gave Donald Trump another chance to move his New York hush-money case to federal court.
And speaking at the Justice Department, President Trump called for faster federal executions and went after California Governor Gavin Newsom over his death-row commutations.

Also, a judge unsealed documents about the search of Representative Ilhan Omar's home. The Democratic National Committee plans a dozen presidential primary debates starting in June twenty twenty-seven, ahead of twenty twenty-eight.

segments.strap: ICE ARRESTS KEEP DRAWING PROTEST
segments.headline: Seattle airport and a Princeton researcher

stats.label: Seattle-Tacoma
stats.value: Father and daughter arrested; protests continue

stats.label: Princeton researcher
stats.value: Eva Yi Xie in ICE custody after Reagan National detention

lines.text: The outrage over the ICE arrest of a father and daughter at Seattle-Tacoma airport continues. Five outlets still carry it. As we said yesterday, ICE says it was a visa overstay.

A second case. A.P. reports Princeton researcher Eva Yi Xie is in ICE custody after being detained while trying to board a flight at Washington National Airport. Her lawyer gave an account of her immigration case. We are reporting that as the lawyer's account.

segments.strap: ARMY TO DETONATE TOXIC MATERIAL IN IOWA WEDNESDAY
segments.headline: Lead azide plan rescheduled; health worries remain

stats.label: Courts
stats.value: Appeals court allowed an emergency permit

sources.name: NBC News (Army moves forward despite concerns)

lines.text: The Army says it has rescheduled a controlled detonation of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant for Wednesday, November twenty-fifth. A.P. says it is sixty-eight barrels, in Middletown, after an appeals court allowed an emergency permit.

Headlines differ on what President Trump did. The Guardian says he deferred to the appeals court. Al Jazeera says he postponed it. We could not read both pages in full, so we will say it plainly: as of now, the plan is for Wednesday, and it had not happened at our capture time.
NBC says the Army is moving forward despite major health concerns. Lead azide is a toxic explosive material. We will cover it when we know more.

segments.strap: CROWDSTRIKE TO BUY ZSCALER FOR ABOUT $44 BILLION
segments.headline: Deals and money, Tuesday

stats.label: Fed's Williams
stats.value: Further rate hikes possible if inflation stays high

lines.text: CrowdStrike agreed to acquire Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at about forty-three point nine billion dollars. Zscaler holders would get one point one three five CrowdStrike shares per share. It still needs to clear closing conditions. That is from the filing.

Amazon said it is bringing in A.I.-inference technology and the team from Israeli startup Decart. The Times of Israel reports the price at seven point five billion dollars. Amazon did not give a price in what we read.

In crypto, the Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture action seeking more than one point one billion dollars in USDC. It alleges North Korean actors stole it from Binance in October. That is an allegation, not a judgment. And Strategy says it bought four hundred fifty-seven bitcoin at about sixty-four thousand nine hundred dollars each.

On rates, New York Fed President John Williams said persistently high inflation could require further rate increases, depending on data. Sweden's Riksbank held at one point seven five percent and Norway's central bank held at four point two five, both leaving a hike possible.

segments.strap: STATES SUE SPACEX OVER GROK ABUSE IMAGES
segments.headline: A.I. lawsuits, safety talk and a cyberattack

stats.label: Lawsuit
stats.value: Virginia and Oregon sue SpaceX over Grok

stats.label: U.N. chief
stats.value: Wants global A.I. safety framework in a year

stats.label: OpenRouter
stats.value: Warns of possible third-party access to MiniMax-routed prompts

lines.text: Virginia and Oregon are suing Elon Musk's SpaceX over Grok, the A.I. chatbot. The states say it created child sexual abuse images and videos. That is the states' allegation in court filings reported by CNBC and Al Jazeera. SpaceX's response was not in what we read.
U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres wants the world to agree on a global A.I. safety framework within a year. Maintain control, he said.

On security, Axios reports OpenRouter warned customers that prompts and responses routed to China's MiniMax may have been accessed by a third party between July and October. Access was not verified. The European Commission warned users of its EU Academy of a data leak after an A.I.-driven cyberattack. And the N.S.A. says it is largely back to normal after several days of internal network disruption.

Perplexity also reports the F.B.I. is investigating an apparent hack of its national criminal-justice database. That is a press report. In happier news, Meta's new shopping agent, Muse, can now do your Black Friday shopping at Walmart. Your wallet, your agent, your problem.

segments.strap: COP31 ENDS WITHOUT A DEAL
segments.headline: Antalya talks split on fossil fuels and money

sources.name: The Verge (A.I. data centers and the talks)

lines.text: The C.O.P. thirty-one climate summit in Antalya ended without a universal political agreement. Countries split over fossil-fuel language and climate finance, according to France twenty-four and Ars Technica.

Twenty-five countries did endorse a wildlife-and-climate declaration, championed by Zimbabwe. A small win in a big loss. And The Verge says A.I. data centers added another wrench to the talks, because of their electricity use.

segments.strap: EU PROPOSES SWEEPING NEW RUSSIA SANCTIONS
segments.headline: Europe: sanctions, bomb threats and courts

stats.label: 22nd sanctions package
stats.value: Banks, crypto, 70+ shadow-fleet ships, sports; not yet approved

lines.text: The European Commission proposed its twenty-second package of Russia sanctions. It targets banks, crypto and payment networks, more than seventy shadow-fleet vessels, and Russian participation in sports and cultural events. All twenty-seven members must agree, so it is a proposal, not law.
Police in Germany and Denmark are investigating bomb threats against schools. No details on who sent them. Al Jazeera and Deutsche Welle report it.

In Spain, the Supreme Court's criminal chamber archived the embezzlement case against Catalan leader Carles Puigdemont and two others under the amnesty law, per RTVE. In Canada, a Quebec court struck down a law that let lawmakers skip the oath to the monarch. The new separatist premier says he will appeal.
In France, Gisèle Pelicot says she is deeply shocked after nude images were used to promote a book. She is suing the publisher, France twenty-four reports.

segments.strap: MEXICO TO TRY 'EL CHAPO ISIDRO' DESPITE U.S. REQUEST
segments.headline: Americas: a drug lord, a drone and Haiti

stats.label: Mexico
stats.value: Alleged drug lord to be tried at home

stats.label: Colombia
stats.value: Drone attack on police base hurts civilians

sources.name: Al Jazeera (Mexico will try El Chapo Isidro)

lines.text: Mexico says it will try the alleged drug lord known as El Chapo Isidro at home, despite a U.S. extradition request. France twenty-four and A.P. report the U.S. flew a surveillance drone over Mexico to help in the capture.

In Colombia, a drone attack on a police base injured civilians, including an infant, and damaged homes. And El Salvador's president Nayib Bukele shared details on how three Salvadoran soldiers died during the Haiti intervention.
Tajikistan has moved to leave the International Criminal Court. It is the fourth country to withdraw since the U.S. diplomatic push against the court, Al Jazeera reports.

segments.strap: CDC: LOCAL MPOX TRANSMISSION IN THE U.S.
segments.headline: Health: mpox, Ebola totals and an F.D.A. approval

stats.label: Mpox (CDC)
stats.value: Recent U.S. clade I cases show local clade Ib spread; risk to public low

stats.label: Ebola (CDC)
stats.value: 11,793 confirmed cases, 5,779 deaths as of Nov. 20

stats.label: F.D.A.
stats.value: Approves Welgemda for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy 2I/R9

lines.text: The C.D.C. says most recently identified U.S. clade one mpox cases had no reported international travel. That points to local transmission of clade Ib. The agency still rates the risk to the general public as low.

On Ebola, the C.D.C. now counts eleven thousand seven hundred ninety-three confirmed cases and five thousand seven hundred seventy-nine deaths, as of November twentieth. Fighting near a hospital in eastern Congo disrupted the response and forced emergency teams into shelter.
And the F.D.A. approved Welgemda, the first treatment for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type two I, R nine, in patients weighing at least thirty kilograms.

segments.strap: COASTAL FLOOD WARNING AND THANKSGIVING TRAVEL
segments.headline: Weather and travel before Thanksgiving

stats.label: San Francisco Bay
stats.value: Coastal flood warning through Thursday; surf 20-30 ft

lines.text: The National Weather Service keeps a coastal flood warning in effect through Thursday around San Francisco. Tides run about two point six feet above normal Tuesday and two point eight feet Wednesday. High surf of twenty to thirty feet is forecast.

Thanksgiving travel. AAA projects eighty-one point five million Americans will go at least fifty miles. A.P. says weather risks touch parts of the East and West coasts. And Delta's weight-and-balance automation failed Sunday, forcing manual workarounds and more than one thousand delays. Delta said operations were stable Monday.
In South Africa, weather warnings call for severe thunderstorms, hail and flash-flood risk around KwaZulu-Natal and Johannesburg. Those are warnings, not a measured toll.

segments.strap: WASHINGTON BEATS CINCINNATI 22-20 ON MONDAY NIGHT
segments.headline: Monday Night Football, the 2031 Women's World Cup and more

lines.text: Washington beat Cincinnati twenty-two to twenty on Monday Night Football, per NFL dot com. Tonight's NBA injury report lists Detroit's Cade Cunningham probable, with Jalen Duren out, and Orlando's Paolo Banchero out.

FIFA announced the United States will host the twenty thirty-one Women's World Cup. And the Court of Arbitration for Sport is expected to rule today on Senegal's appeal over the African Cup of Nations final. In soccer, Brentford beat Everton four to nothing. In cricket, New Zealand drew the first Test with India.

segments.strap: ALSO TODAY
segments.headline: Quick hits

graphic.title: Quick hits
bullets: Amazon drone hits fiber cable, garage in Michigan; F.A.A. probe
Indonesia candy factory fire: 34 workers missing
Istanbul hunts animal resembling a lion in woodland
Shenzhou-24 launch set for Wednesday, with Pakistani astronaut

sources.name: Times of Israel (Mossad and Taylor Swift plot)

lines.text: Quick hits. An Amazon delivery drone struck a Michigan fiber cable and a garage. The F.A.A. is investigating. In Indonesia, the search continues for thirty-four workers missing after a candy factory fire. More remains were recovered.

The World Food Programme warns wars are choking global food routes and threatening aid for seven point three million people. Turkish police are searching an Istanbul woodland for an animal resembling a lion.

China names the Shenzhou twenty-four crew for a Wednesday launch, including Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who would be the first foreign astronaut aboard China's station. And a former Mossad chief says the agency helped foil an ISIS plot at a twenty twenty-four Taylor Swift show.

Last, a Don Toliver concert in Manchester was evacuated over an unknown substance, possibly tear gas, and a head-on crash in Ohio killed two bus drivers and hurt nine. Pope Francis's diaries, per ABC, reveal a two-year spiritual crisis that included visions of the devil.

lines.text: That's Heartbeat News for Tuesday. A new show every day by morning. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. A boss comes back, tankers burn, and a satellite warning hangs over us. Two sides in every account. We will tell you what happened, and who said it. Take care of each other.
